proof_review: For an inclusion-minimal transitive family on two invariant sets, one selected deletion-eligible edge per mark forms a forest. At t=m1+m2-2 it has exactly the two full invariant sets as tree components. Every additional transposition of a member has its endpoints joined by a selected path. If that path contains any different colour l, replacing that selected l edge by the additional edge and the rest of the path contradicts deletion eligibility for l. Thus the only transposition of that member is its own selected edge. This is an argument about actual involutions on the stated sets, not about abstract independent generating families.

At 2r=n+2 the full chain from the orbit-budget proof is saturated: r-1-|M|<=c1+c2-2<=k1+k2-2 and |M|<=m1+m2-2, together with the final product-size bound. Hence |M|=m1+m2-2 and cj=kj separately. The block-image family is inclusion-minimal for transitivity, so the new lemma applies to its actual images.

Its two trees are paths, since three incident transpositions are pairwise noncommuting and their distinct integer labels cannot be pairwise consecutive. Along each path all labels are consecutive with a fixed direction. A crossing block cannot be internal: its incident labels would both have to be i-1 and i+1, but these commute. The crossing blocks are therefore endpoints. The two incident labels are distinct because each mark in M is a transposition on only one of the block sets. This forces the exact two intervals ending at i-1 and starting at i+1, after reversing orientation.

Every M-point orbit meets all blocks on its side. There are exactly kj such orbits in mj*kj points, so each orbit has exactly mj points and meets every block once. Projection to the block set is an equivariant bijection for every orbit. Thus block-trivial elements of M fix all actual points, and the marks from one block path fix the entire opposite side. No unproved action of later marks on these point orbits is asserted.

Each remaining mark has label outside the full interval M union {i} and fixes both crossing endpoints, hence the two crossing blocks. On either original block system it centralizes the natural symmetric block action except possibly its far-end path transposition. For mj>=3 the remaining S_(mj-1) has one nontrivial orbit containing the crossing block; a commuting permutation fixes that block and then the whole orbit, with the remaining block fixed too. For mj=2 fixing one of two blocks suffices. This proves the actual remaining block image is trivial, including all small mj boundaries.

Only after that block-image step does the proof contract actual M-point orbits. The remaining selected ambient-eligible edges form two spanning trees by exact equality of their count. A nontrivial transposition of a remaining mark lies inside one original block, and therefore joins distinct M-point orbits because each meets that block once. Any selected-tree path between its contracted endpoints containing another colour gives an actual path avoiding that colour through M-orbits and the extra edge, contradicting ambient eligibility. Thus every transposition of the mark joins the same selected pair of point orbits and lies on the same side. This uses actual paths; no permutation action or IP on a point-orbit quotient is assumed.

Every omission mark is now supported on exactly one side. Along each consecutive interval of labels that side cannot change without adjacent marks commuting and disconnecting the parent diagram. The already identified neighbours i-1 and i+1 fix the direction. Hence the saturated two-imprimitive cut is perfect. The argument also shows that such saturation cannot occur at an endpoint index, since both different neighbouring block-path labels would be required.

The changed rank hypothesis is audited precisely. Under 2r>n+1, the only possible both-imprimitive case allowed by 2r<=n+2 is equality 2r=n+2, and it is now perfect. Interior singletons and the two-point disconnected primitive-image exception have bounds n+1 and n respectively. The first five head lemmas are independent of the rank range; their wrong-side or final-shared conclusion n>=2r is still impossible. The fixed-point count and support placement therefore hold in this wider range without importing an unproved equality classification.

The previously accepted strict split routing only used the stronger numerical assumption at steps explicitly rechecked here: all-paired gives n, paired first tail gives n+1, wrong second orientation gives n, and separated cuts with g<=h give n>=2r+h-g. All remain contradictions. Thus the same sets X,Y and indices h<g with X union Y equal to Omega are obtained. For nonempty middle interval retain its c>=1 proper-orbit deficit to obtain 2r<=n+1. For empty middle interval g=h+1, rho_h belongs to the Y-group and rho_(h+1) to the X-group; their noncommutation forces intersecting supports. Keeping this positive overlap again gives 2r<=n+1. The r-1-g reversal and +4 identity remain exact.

The concluding wing use is conditional on its stated actual hypotheses. In the application at a perfect parent split, the two wing index families are disjoint; a transitive omission inside one wing, together with the other full wing and the crossing mark, would make the corresponding parent omission transitive. This supplies inherited omission intransitivity. The packet does not itself establish a trivial internal split factor, leaf-kernel conditions, pure end mark or principal stability bijection.
